name: AnyMachine (agent-built rigged machines in Blender)
summary: MIT repo documenting a pipeline where a coding agent builds machines in Blender Python: reference sheets first, then part-by-part modeling, rigging and animation, with renders checked against the references. Includes build scripts, notes and exported GLBs: a 30 m stilt walker (160 parts, 104 bones, hydraulics, 3 animations), a helicopter, lifeboat station, oil-rig props, light fixtures, plus rigged laptop/quadruped/backpack experiments with 0-1 joint parameters.

access.notes: README status: experiments, no endpoint yet; models are simpler than their reference sheets in places. Requires Blender and an agent (author used Claude Code) to reproduce.

procedure: Read PIPELINE.md (part 1 machines, part 2 complex static objects)
Clone or download the repo zip
Run a build script such as stilt/build_stilt.py in Blender, or import the provided GLBs (e.g. stilt/stilt.glb)

stats.count: 6 experiments (stilt, hardsurface, laptop, quadruped, spider, backpacks)

verdict.why: Concrete, reproducible agent-to-Blender method with real scripts and rigged GLB outputs under MIT; differs from mesh generators by building clean part-based rigs. Still experimental.

image.alt: Concept painting of a tall four-legged stilt walker beside the agent-built Blender model with a small human figure for scale
